rules.title: Do not use browser APIs in Nitro server files
rules.description: Browser globals are unavailable in Nitro server runtime.
rules.why: Nitro code can run in Node, edge, or worker runtimes where browser APIs such as window, document, and localStorage do not exist.
rules.recommendedReplacement: Use request/event data, server utilities, or move browser work to app client code.

rules.title: Do not use app composables in Nitro server files
rules.description: Nuxt app composables are not available from Nitro server files.
rules.why: Server handlers run with Nitro request context, not Vue setup context. App composables like useRoute(), useFetch(), and useHead() depend on the Nuxt app runtime.
rules.recommendedReplacement: Use event-aware Nitro utilities in server handlers.

rules.title: Do not use navigateTo in Nitro routes
rules.description: Nitro handlers should redirect with server response utilities instead of Nuxt app navigation.
rules.why: navigateTo() is a Nuxt app navigation helper. Nitro handlers need to write an HTTP redirect response for the current request event.
rules.recommendedReplacement: Use sendRedirect(event, path) in Nitro handlers.

rules.title: Do not use useNuxtApp in Nitro routes
rules.description: Nitro handlers run outside the Nuxt app runtime, so useNuxtApp() is unavailable.
rules.why: Nitro request handlers execute in the server runtime with an event object, not inside Vue or Nuxt app setup. App composables rely on Nuxt app instance state that does not exist there.
rules.recommendedReplacement: Use event-aware Nitro, h3, or server utilities that receive the request event.

rules.title: Use assertMethod for single-method handlers
rules.description: Single-method Nitro handlers should use the H3 method assertion helper instead of ad hoc method checks.
rules.recommendedReplacement: Use assertMethod(event, "POST") for handlers that accept one HTTP method.

rules.title: Use event.$fetch in Nitro handlers
rules.description: Proxy internal API calls through event.$fetch() when request context matters.
rules.why: $fetch() does not automatically carry request-scoped context such as headers, cookies, or event context. event.$fetch() preserves the current Nitro request context for internal server calls.
rules.recommendedReplacement: Use event.$fetch() when proxying to other server routes from a Nitro handler.

rules.title: Use request IP utilities instead of raw IP headers
rules.description: Request-sensitive Nitro code should not trust client-controlled forwarding headers directly.
rules.recommendedReplacement: Use the H3/Nitro request IP utility and centralize trusted proxy handling instead of reading IP headers directly.

rules.title: Use readValidatedBody for validated request bodies
rules.description: When a Nitro handler validates a request body, read and validate it through the H3 utility.
rules.why: Raw request input and validation can drift apart when they are separate operations. Nitro and h3 provide validated helpers that keep parsing and validation coupled at the request boundary.
rules.recommendedReplacement: Use readValidatedBody(event, validator) instead of readBody(event) followed by separate validation.

examples.title: Keep reading and validation together

rules.title: Use getValidatedQuery for validated query strings
rules.description: When a Nitro handler validates query input, read and validate it through the H3 utility.
rules.why: Raw request input and validation can drift apart when they are separate operations. Nitro and h3 provide validated helpers that keep parsing and validation coupled at the request boundary.
rules.recommendedReplacement: Use getValidatedQuery(event, validator) instead of getQuery(event) followed by separate validation.

examples.title: Keep reading and validation together

rules.title: Use getValidatedRouterParams for validated route params
rules.description: When a Nitro handler validates route params, read and validate them through the H3 utility.
rules.why: Raw request input and validation can drift apart when they are separate operations. Nitro and h3 provide validated helpers that keep parsing and validation coupled at the request boundary.
rules.recommendedReplacement: Use getValidatedRouterParams(event, validator) instead of getRouterParams(event) followed by separate validation.

examples.title: Keep reading and validation together

rules.title: Pass event to useRuntimeConfig in server handlers
rules.description: Read runtime config with the Nitro event inside server handlers.
rules.why: Passing the event lets Nitro resolve request-aware runtime config consistently in server code.
